intent: A line the length of the planet: the migration route draws itself from Greenland down the Atlantic to the Antarctic ice edge at the reveal, a tern sticker flies the whole S-curve while the yearly counter climbs to 70,000 km, a whale sticker gets a much shorter line for scale, and a pin lands on the Antarctic feeding ground with the two-summers card.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which animal makes the LONGEST migration?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which animal makes the longest migration?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat
lines.text: Humpback whale, Monarch butterfly, or Arctic tern?
The Arctic tern. Pole to pole and back, every single year.

lines.direction: hold the whole Atlantic; the short blue whale route draws on 'humpback' with a whale sticker; on 'tern' the tern sticker takes off and flies the full yellow S-curve while the counter runs to 70,000; a dizzy sticker on 'year'
lines.text: A humpback swims about 8,000 kilometres each way. The tern zigzags around 70,000 a year.

lines.direction: hold wide; Greenland pulses with its tag and a sun sticker on 'breeds'; the winter-feeding pin and the ice-edge tag land on 'Antarctic' with an ice sticker; the 2 SUMMERS card and a second sun on 'daylight'
lines.text: It breeds in the Arctic summer, then feeds at the Antarctic ice. More daylight than any animal alive.

lines.direction: drift north a little; a soap sticker on 'weighs'; the 2.4 MILLION KM card on 'lifetime' as the route re-draws itself fast; a moon sticker on 'Moon' with a rocket; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: It weighs about 100 grams. In a lifetime it covers 3 trips to the Moon and back.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Lighter than a bar of soap. Follow us.
